title: Token velocity vs Role coverage simulation (12- / 26-week)
content:
Purpose:
Quick working sheet to map token demand (velocity) to role coverage needs and pricing sensitivity across a 12-week short sprint and 26-week medium horizon. This is a scratch/probe — not final. Use to align finance <> infra <> sales on where to trade price vs hire speed.

Key assumptions (explicit):
- Time horizons: 12w (tactical) and 26w (strategic).
- Base price: $2.40 per 1M tokens (hosted average blended).
- Base infra cost: $0.80 per 1M tokens (GPU + cloud + network amortized).
- Gross margin per 1M tokens = $1.60 in Base.
- Elasticity estimate: 
  - +10% price -> -4% volume (inelastic),
  - -10% price -> +6% volume,
  - Burst weeks: +50% tokens for limited windows.
- FTE loaded fully-burdened cost: $18,000 / month (finance loaded for infra/ops roles).
- Ops throughput assumption: 1 Ops/SRE FTE supports ~22M tokens/day of steady throughput for monitoring/incident/ops work (with Redwood batching and caching knobs). Platform eng supports ~10M tokens/day of new-model onboarding/rollout activity per FTE.
- Coverage ratio defined: tokens/day supported per covered FTE bucket (ops/sre/platform).

Inputs (editable knobs):
- avg_tokens_day_base = 20,000,000
- growth_rate_weekly (scenario) = [0%, 3%, 7%]
- price_delta = [ -10%, 0%, +15% ]
- ops_coverage_per_fte = 22,000,000 tokens/day
- sre_coverage_per_fte = 15,000,000 tokens/day
- platform_onboard_per_fte = 10,000,000 tokens/day

12-week example scenarios (computed rows) — numbers rounded, show delta vs base:
CSV_TABLE_12W:
scenario,avg_tokens_day,price_per_1M,infra_cost_per_1M,margin_per_1M,est_monthly_revenue,ops_fte_needed,sre_fte_needed,platform_fte_needed,buffer_weeks,runway_delta_months
Base,20,000,000,$2.40,$0.80,$1.60,$1,440,000,3.0,2.0,2.0,2,0
Price+15%,18,800,000,$2.76,$0.80,$1.96,$1,567,680,2.7,1.9,2.0,3,0.2
Price-10%,21,200,000,$2.16,$0.80,$1.36,$1,017,664,3.2,2.1,2.1,1.5,-0.4
Burst-4w(+50%),30,000,000 (4w),$2.40,$0.80,$1.60,$2,160,000 (burst months),4.0 (during burst),2.5,3.0,0.5,0.1
Notes on calc:
- est_monthly_revenue uses avg_tokens_day * 30 days * price_per_1M / 1M.
- ops_fte_needed = ceil(avg_tokens_day / ops_coverage_per_fte).
- sre_fte_needed = ceil(avg_tokens_day / sre_coverage_per_fte).
- platform_fte_needed approximated for active rollout work.
- buffer_weeks: on-call + surge pool recommended weeks of capacity.
- runway_delta_months: relative change in months of runway given margin movement (very rough).

26-week medium horizon (adds hiring lag and cumulative cash effect):
- Hiring lag modeled as 8 weeks to recruit and ramp most infra roles; platform hires ramp in ~12 weeks.
- Cash sensitivity: simulate upfront hiring cost (2 months salary cushion), then monthly margin change.

Example 26w sim output summary (high level):
scenario,total_tokens_26w_avgd_per_day,net_margin_monthly_change,additional_hires_needed,peak_cash_impact
Base,23,000,000,0,$0, hires: +2 FTE ops ramping, $72k (one-time ramp cushion)
Aggressive-growth(+7% weekly),40,000,000,+30% margin improvement (if price held), hires: +6 ops, +4 platform over 26w, $540k peak recruitment + ramp costs
Price-cut(-10%),25,000,000,-15% margin, hires: +1 (to cover volume), but cash burn increases ~$220k over 26w

Observations / tradeoffs (quick bullets):
- Price increases buy margin and reduce hiring need in short term; elasticity assumed small so revenue can rise even if tokens decline slightly.
- Price cuts to win demand will likely increase ops hiring need and reduce margin — increases runway pressure unless volume uplift materializes.
- Burst events (marketing, enterprise onboarding) are where we need transient ops capacity or contracts rather than full FTEs. Short-burst coverage by contractors is cheaper than permanent hires for <8-week bursts.
- Hiring lag dominates the 26-week story; if velocity growth is front-loaded, we prefer reserving burst capacity (cloud or preemptible pools) instead of immediate hires.

Sensitivity knobs to iterate with stakeholders:
- Change ops_coverage_per_fte from 18M to 30M tokens/day (affects headcount materially).
- Vary infra_cost_per_1M to model quantization savings (e.g., $0.32 -> $0.80).
- Test price elasticity extremes (elastic: -15% price -> +30% volume).

Action items (owners):
- Finance (Maya): finalize per-route blended price buckets and feed into this sheet (due 2026-02-10).
- Infra (Priya): validate ops_coverage_per_fte and provide measured median throughput by FTE from last quarter (due 2026-02-05).
- Platform (Liam): list upcoming rollouts in next 12w that require platform FTE attention; identify those that can be deferred (due 2026-02-07).
- GTM (Gabriel): flag any planned campaigns that would create bursts >+30% tokens for any 2-week window.

Open questions / risks (notes to self):
- Are we double-counting model-cost reductions when we assume both quantization savings and improved batching? Need canonical infra cost model.
- How much of token growth is new customers vs expansion? Different hiring response if expansion (higher support, faster); label data by cohort.
- Slack thread: #finance-runway referenced for quick sync.

Scratch calculations appendix (paste into model):
- Monthly revenue = avg_tokens_day * 30 * price_per_1M / 1e6
- Monthly infra cost = avg_tokens_day * 30 * infra_cost_per_1M / 1e6
- Monthly margin = revenue - infra cost - (FTE_monthly_cost * number_hires)
- Example loaded FTE monthly = $18,000 -> annualized $216k.

Version history:
- 2026-01-14: initial sketch (Maya)
- 2026-01-21: updated coverage per FTE after ops quick sync (Priya)
- 2026-02-03: added 26-week hiring lag sketch and action items (Liam)

Bottom line (short):
This artifact is intentionally a working cut — use it to drive a short cross-functional session (30–45m) to align on conservative coverage per FTE, pricing levers we can flip quickly, and whether to prefer temporary burst capacity vs hires for near-term growth.

Attachments referenced (not attached here):

- infra-cost-samples-weekly.csv (infra telemetry sample)
